title: Interactions in Ecosystems
seo_title: Grade 7 Ecosystem Interactions Worksheets: Predation, Competition and Symbiosis
standard_text: Construct an explanation that predicts patterns of interactions among organisms across multiple ecosystems.
meta_desc: Free middle school science worksheets on interactions in ecosystems (NGSS MS-LS2-2): competition, predation, mutualism, commensalism and parasitism, and predator-prey cycles. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: Organisms compete, hunt and help each other.
key_sub: Predation, competition, mutualism, commensalism and parasitism happen in every ecosystem and affect population sizes.
body_html:
How to think about it

Organisms interact in patterns that repeat in every ecosystem:

  • Competition: organisms need the same limited resource.
  • Predation: a predator hunts and eats prey.
  • Mutualism: both benefit (bees and flowers).
  • Commensalism: one benefits, the other is not helped or harmed (barnacles on a whale).
  • Parasitism: one benefits, the other is harmed (ticks on a dog).

Predator and prey populations often rise and fall in cycles: when prey increase, predators increase a little later; then prey decrease, and predators follow.

Example

Oxpeckers eat ticks off zebras. Both benefit. Which interaction?

Both benefit.

Answer: mutualism

Example

Wolves are removed. What happens to deer at first?

Less predation.

Answer: They increase.

Common mistakes

  • Mixing up commensalism (one is unaffected) and parasitism (one is harmed).
  • Thinking more predators lead to more prey.
  • Thinking parasites always kill their hosts quickly.

faq.q: What are the three types of symbiosis?
faq.a: Mutualism (both benefit), commensalism (one benefits, the other is not affected) and parasitism (one benefits, the other is harmed).
When prey increase, predators have more food and increase; then prey decrease, and predators decrease after them.

faq.q: Why do the same kinds of interactions happen in different ecosystems?
faq.a: All organisms need resources, so they compete, eat others or cooperate in similar ways everywhere.
